column1: # Stores that claim durability, and what each does when it cannot be durable (preview.25 evaluation P25-M2, 2026-10-21).
# A store that claims durability either refuses to start when its path is unusable, or requires an explicit opt-out
# that the operator states in configuration; a silent fallback to memory is the defect class this table pins.
# `test` names a Go test in the public Core (cloud/...; checked by spec/tools/spec_durable_stores_check.py as a
# `func Test...(` in that package) or `untested` — an untested row is a gap reported by the checker, not a pass.

column4: refuses to start: REPORT_QUEUE_NOT_DURABLE (exit via the config refusal); memory only requires PAIL_REPORT_QUEUE_BYTES=0
a fatal (E-STOP) report is written to fatal-<key>.wal before its upstream attempt and re-queued by the next run

issuer-first: a record is announced only after it is durable, and a token is not issued when its journal record cannot be appended; segments rotate at 64 MiB or 24 h (writer defaults) and are never deleted by the Issuer; retention, archival and disk monitoring are the operator's responsibility (owner decision 2026-10-29): move whole segments to an archive (the verifier reports a missing older segment as a NOTE and keeps verifying the rest), and watch free space — a full disk stops issuance (no token without a durable record), never the ledger's integrity; measured growth under the single contract: about 1.5 MB per TurtleBot3 judge run, about 45 MB per hour of continuous judging (preview.39 evaluation P39-N1)
untested: whether an unwritable state file refuses the bundle pull is not pinned
requires persistent storage; refuses unusable storage; critical fault blocks new token serving

column2: rejection quarantine (rejected-<hash>.json beside the report log)
column4: bounded to 4096 entries / 16 MiB (preview.35 evaluation P35-L2); beyond the bound a refused observation is counted (refusedNotRetained) and not retained, a refused effect report (fatal, step_complete) raises the critical fault that blocks new token serving; the queue advances in every case; a memory-only queue requires PAIL_REPORT_QUEUE_BYTES=0 and retains nothing

refuses to start: S23 when the directory cannot hold the serving model's bytes under their SHA-256, or already holds different bytes under that name (not overwritten); the collector re-hashes every snapshot it reads and does not use one whose content does not hash to its name (zone_resolution=unresolved, never today's model)
